title: Docsite overhaul: pragmatic usage patterns, examples, and migration recipes for core UI primitives
creator: Sophia Patel
description: Overhaul and consolidate documentation for core design primitives (tokens, buttons, tables, charts) with a strong emphasis on pragmatic usage patterns, explicit do/don't examples, migration recipes for teams moving from legacy tokens/components, and machine-readable API snippets for devs. Goal: reduce support/clarity tickets, improve adoption of new token semantics, and provide clear migration steps for products on Dedicated/Private deployments that need strict auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Top-level doc pages for Tokens, Buttons, Tables, Charts exist with consistent structure: Purpose, When to use, When not to use, API, Examples, Migration notes
Each component page includes 3 pragmatic usage examples (compact, default, data-heavy) with code snippets (JSX + token reference)
Migration recipes cover: legacy token maps -> new semantic tokens, deprecated props, and migration PR checklist
Design and engineering have signed off on component API snippets and test harnesses (links to PRs and E2E fixtures)
Docs rendered in staging, accessible from Console sidebar, and smoke-tested for mobile/responsive layouts
tasks: Audit existing component docs and collect high-traffic queries from support (Connor, GH issue list)
Draft standardized page template and token glossary (copy + token usage matrix)
Create 3 example variants per component and obtain engineering-ready snippets
Run migration walkthrough with two internal product teams and capture checklist items
Coordinate with Docs Eng to add structured metadata for search and deprecation notices
Implement staging deployment and manual QA pass on Chrome/Firefox/Safari + mobile

decision_log: Decision: Use a standardized 'Pattern Card' on each page (visual + code + tradeoffs) to speed reader comprehension. Trade-off: increases initial authoring overhead but reduces repeated support questions.
Decision: Publish migration recipes as a separate collapsible section to avoid cluttering usage examples for new authors.

Decision: Use semantic token names in examples rather than raw color/spacing values to accelerate adoption of new token semantics. Engineering validated that runtime substitution is safe for Dedicated customers.
